A design philosophy with a small working example

One story appears in a menu, a row and a story page. Some words come from the same source. The menu also has its own label.

Open the workshop and try changing each value. Watch which views change and which keep their wording. You can open the code if you want more detail. Your edits stay in that tab and reset when you reload.

Words used here
source
Where a statement or displayed value comes from: for example, a document, a record or a piece of code.
projection
A particular view of the same thing. In the workshop, one story can appear as a page, a menu link or a row.
overlay
A local change to a view. In the workshop, the menu can use its own label while the story keeps its title.
Read the fuller explanation

Start with a story called “What happened”. A web menu calls it “The story”; a row follows the original title. Change one of those values and see what follows—and what keeps its own wording.

The living infographic opens the route from meaning to types, projections, contextual overlays, algebra and HTML. An edit returns to its declared source, then the checked process rebuilds and verifies the visible result.

This is a small working example of a larger intention: remove unnecessary labour, preserve human authorship, and make the consequences understandable and the evidence inspectable. You can read its rules and source. General programme editing and a complete authoring environment remain future work.

Where this comes from: People choosing; machines helping

Product philosophy · inspectable example

A design philosophy with a small working example

The workshop lets you edit two values and follow the results through the existing checking system. It is not a complete authoring environment or independent verification.

Read the full source note

Human authorship, assisted by AI

Developed with Aaron in the Encounter discussion: remove unnecessary labour, preserve human authorship, and make consequences and evidence inspectable. Autonomy, human taste and risk-appropriate assurance are design commitments. The accompanying example executes a bounded typed edit through the existing Temple kernel. Its checks do not establish independent verification, a complete authoring environment, employment outcomes or a measured productivity multiplier.

This account is drawn from Aaron’s own words; it is not an independent account of anyone else’s experience.
